answer: To mitigate fake-identity attacks, an economy of AI agents can employ a Sybil-resistance mechanism based on a distributed graph structure, where each agent represents a vertex and forms connections with its peers. By periodically executing a "comet" event, where a random subset of vertices are temporarily isolated, the network can detect and prevent Sybil attacks. As a thread of malicious activity is severed, the network can quickly adapt and re-establish connections with legitimate agents, thus maintaining the integrity of the consensus.
